newsitem.title: USA: Michigan police break up Kevorkian consultation.
newsitem.headline: Michigan police break up Kevorkian consultation.

text.p: Police stormed into a hotel room and broke up a counselling session between Dr. Jack Kevorkian and a 60-year-old California woman, a lawyer for the the assisted suicide advocate said late on Friday.

Kevorkian and one of his assistants were talking with Isabelle Correa of Fresno, California, on Friday when police and attorneys from the Oakland County, Michigan, prosecutors office entered Correa's hotel room in the Detroit suburb of Bloomfield Township, said Geoffrey Fieger, Kevorkian's attorney.

An irate Fieger told reporters at a hastily called news conference that Correa, who has a spinal injury and is in constant pain, travelled to Michigan with members of her family to meet Kevorkian. It was her first session with Kevorkian and the 68-year-old retired pathologist had not made a decision on whether to help her die, Fieger said.
But Correa told reporters she came to Michigan to end her life with Kevorkian's help. Kevorkian has acknowledged being present at 39 assisted suicides since 1990.
"I came to die, and it's so sad that I have to come across the United States to see a man like Kevorkian when there should be one in California," said Correa.

Fieger charged that between "20 and 30" police and prosecutors in marked and unmarked vehicles came into Correa's room after renting a nearby room. "They had rented the room next to Mrs. Correa's. They had staked her out," he said.
Police later took Correa's pain medication and rosary, Fieger said. He added he planned to file charges against authorities.
Correa said she planned to stay in Michigan and consult with Kevorkian.

It was the first time that police have disrupted a Kevorkian consultation since he began his assisted suicide crusade six years ago. Representatives from the Bloomfield Township police and Oakland County Sheriff's office either would not comment or could not be reached.
Juries at three separate trials have acquitted Kevorkian on assisted suicide charges over the last two years.
